text:
marie: Heads-up — monitoring showed an ECC anomaly cluster in apac-gpupool-3 starting ~2050-01-23T09:01Z. 8 cards with rising correctable counts, not all at same rack. I want to discuss thresholds and whether to trigger a soft-drain or escalate to replacement.

monitor-bot: ALERT: ECC_RATE anomaly for apac-gpupool-3 (grouped)
- gpu0: 45 -> 540 CE/min
- gpu2: 12 -> 310 CE/min
- gpu5: 5 -> 220 CE/min
Pattern: short bursts every ~30s, small Xid 43/45 logs. No hard Xid56s yet.
Link: https://internal/mon/alerts/2050012345

sahil: thx. any correlation with kernel updates or rack-level PSU changes?

marie: no kernel changes in the region in last 24h. PSU and pdu telemetry is clean. Noise seems distributed across different host models (a100/gh200 mix).

olga: how noisy is the signal vs baseline? we should avoid auto-evac if it's a transient spike across many cards — that could cause mass capacity loss. can we tighten the detection window?

marie: baseline is ~1-3 CE/min per card. This is sustained >200 CE/min on 3 cards for 10+ minutes and bursty on others. current auto-drain policy: hard-drain at 1000 CE/min sustained 5m OR soft-drain at 300 CE/min 10m.

kai: proposal: add a pattern-detection stage before drain that checks (1) cross-host correlation score, (2) sustained tail of >250 CE/min for 8m, (3) absence of recent config changes. If correlation high across hosts in the same switching domain, prefer gradual evacuation across pool (soft-drain + no immediate replacement) to keep capacity for evictions.

marie: +1. Also propose we run an automated synthetic repro on 1 suspected host: run a short mem-stress and ECC repro script to see if error counters grow deterministically. If repro fails to escalate, continue soft-drain monitoring. If it reproduces, mark for replace.

olga: how would rollout look operationally? if we soft-drain ~1 host every 5m, do we have enough headroom? APAC peak traffic in 30m.

marie: we checked — apac pool has ~15% spare capacity right now. Soft-drain velocity capped at 1 host / 10m by default; canary of 1 host first. If we see task backpressure >70%, pause and notify on-call.

monitor-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance window in apac region at 2050-01-23T11:00Z. Any replacement must avoid that window.

sahil: sounds reasonable. Recommend: lower soft-drain threshold to 200 CE/min for the pattern-detect rule to catch earlier, but require repro+correlation before auto-replace. Also add a cooldown so we don't oscillate.

marie: implemented in draft policy:
```
pattern_detection: {
  correlation_threshold: 0.6,
  sustained_ce_per_card: 200, # per-card threshold
  sustained_window_mins: 8,
  repro_required_for_replace: true,
  soft_drain_rate_limit_mins: 10,
  pause_on_backpressure_pct: 70
}
```

olga: please add a quick dashboard widget with per-pool correlation score and a "predicted impact" gauge so on-call can make a single-click pause.

marie: will add. also adding a small synthetic test job to the runbook: `./tools/ecc_repro --short --run-on host` and a link to the playbook page: https://internal/playbooks/gpu-ecc-pattern

kai: agree with the plan. one extra ask: add a fallback route to route latency-sensitive requests to dedicated-capacity in eu-west if apac degradation hits >30% error budget for 5m.

marie: noted. i'll open a follow-up doc with exact routing rules and the PR for the policy. planning to kick off canary soft-drain in 5m.

sahil: :thumbsup: pls @oncall if it starts auto-evacuating.

marie: pinging on-call in #eng-oncall and will post updates there.

monitor-bot: ACTION: canary soft-drain started on host apac-gpu-102 at 2050012380.

olga: monitoring the dashboards now. if anything spikes beyond plan, we'll abort and roll back the policy.

marie: thanks all. will update thread with outcomes after canary completes.
